archive.delete.message %@: “%@” and all its notes, photos and settings will be removed permanently. This cannot be undone.
archive.delete.title: Delete Forever?
archive.empty.description: Archived projects appear here. You can restore them or delete them for good.
browser.empty.description: Create a project from a 3D model (USDZ) or add the example project.
browser.empty.title: No Projects
browser.rename.title: Rename Project
browser.title: Projects
camera.enterRoom: First person: enter the room in the middle of the view
camera.motionDenied: Free look needs the device's motion sensors – this browser provides none (or access was denied; allow "Motion & Orientation" in the website settings).
chimney.flipSide: Move to Other Side of Wall
circuits.none: No circuit reaches the board – conduits and risers lead the lines here.
common.error.title: Something Went Wrong
composer.hint: After tapping Place, tap where the note should be pinned. You can drag it until you tap Done.
composer.title: New Note
costs.hint: Prices are saved with the project and apply to every element of the same type (also shown in the device properties). Line lengths are measured along the drawn lines.
costs.unplaced.hint: Planned in the Devices tab but not placed in the model yet – counted in the total.
credits.browser.animation: Animations and drawings of the interface (Settings' toys, icons, the project list's background)
credits.browser.clipboard: Copies the debug labels to the clipboard
credits.browser.images: Reading photos, drawing the intro and the focus preview.
credits.browser.render: Running the shared core and 3-D rendering.
credits.browser.services: Keeping the screen awake, intro vibration, intro sounds, free look with the motion sensors.
credits.browser.storage: Storing projects in the browser, offline use.
credits.lang.javascript: Web app user interface, three.js renderer, storage (IndexedDB), service worker.
credits.lang.json: Project files, string catalog (English + German), web app manifest.
credits.lang.swift: Shared core, native app, WebAssembly adapter.
credits.lib.collections: Data structures of FoundationEssentials (bundled copy of swift-collections).
credits.lib.compilerRT: Compiler helper functions (e.g. 64-bit arithmetic on 32-bit WebAssembly).
credits.lib.foundation: Data, JSON and text basics of the shared core in WebAssembly (without ICU).
credits.lib.libcxx: C++ standard library the Swift runtime is built on.
credits.lib.swiftRuntime: Runtime of the shared Swift core, compiled into the WebAssembly module.
credits.lib.three: 3-D rendering in the web app; OrbitControls for the overview camera.
credits.lib.wasiLibc: C library (maths, memory) of the WebAssembly module.
credits.system.modelio: Import of OBJ, PLY, STL and Alembic models.
credits.system.pasteboard: Copies the debug labels to the clipboard
credits.system.pdf: Shows the exported plan in the guided tour.
credits.system.services: Intro sounds, free look with device motion, photo picker.
credits.tool.buildStamp: Gives every build (iOS, macOS, web) the next build number and its build time.
credits.tool.claude: AI coding assistant used for development.
credits.tool.coreTests: Unit tests of the shared core, also on Linux.
credits.tool.cutSounds: Cuts the toddler's pacifier sounds out of a recording (decoded with PyAV).
credits.tool.debugScene: Unpacks the debug bug's scene line into an importable project and its camera
credits.tool.hostWebTests: Runs the guided tour and the browser test on the Mac in Docker (Playwright image, http-server), dispatched through daemon.sh
credits.tool.licenses: Downloads the full licence and notice texts of every web app library, pinned to the versions in the build.
credits.tool.loaderTitle: Writes the web loading screen's brick title from the shared core at build time
credits.tool.poppler: Renders PDF pages to images – to read floor plans such as the installation plan.
credits.tool.provision: Sets up the Linux development VM with all of the above.
credits.tool.publish: Public variant of the web build for GitHub Pages: the app's JavaScript, CSS and HTML minified, obfuscated and without comments
credits.tool.python: Generate test fixtures, the app icon and the intro sounds, check PDF exports, merge translations.
credits.tool.showreel: Records the presentation video: drives the web app with real mouse and keyboard input on a virtual clock, frame by frame (Playwright, FFmpeg), and composes the clips with 3-D moves, frames and type (OpenCV, Pillow, the Inter typeface).
credits.tool.simplifiedExample: Writes the "Simplified model" template from an exported project reworked in the app.
credits.tool.swiftpm: Compiler and package manager of the shared core HausbauCore (no external packages).
credits.tool.tourAssets: Draws the demo wall photo the guided tour attaches.
credits.tool.twoStoreyExample: Writes the two-storey example house (USDZ) from the dimension chains of its floor plans.
credits.tool.wasm: Compiles the shared core to WebAssembly and assembles the web app.
credits.tool.webTests: Smoke test of the WebAssembly module, browser tests and the guided tour as end-to-end test with screenshots in headless Chromium.
credits.tool.xcode: Builds the iOS/iPadOS and macOS apps; daemon.sh builds on the host Mac and takes screenshots on request.
debug.modal.title: Debug Info
debug.scene %lld: scene: %lld KB – the exact scene (model, camera, light), copied with the text
devicePicker.hint: After tapping Place, tap a wall, ceiling or floor. Each tap places another device; drag to move the last one. Tap Done to finish.
devicePicker.title: Place Device
doctor.footer: The Model Doctor checks storeys, walls, rooms and devices. Apply a proposal (undoable) or dismiss an issue. Markers (!) show issues in 3D while this tab is open.
doctor.rule.deviceOutsideRoom: %1$@ is outside the outline of %2$@ (it lies in %3$@).
doctor.rule.ductFull: %1$@: %2$@ cables fill %3$@ percent of its %5$@ mm (at most %4$@ percent).
doctor.rule.storeyOffset: %1$@ is offset from %2$@ by %3$@ m (x) and %4$@ m (z).
doctor.rule.storeySizeMismatch: %1$@ is %3$@ m wide, %2$@ below is %4$@ m wide.
doctor.rule.wallFragment: Wall %1$@ is only a fragment (%2$@ m long).
doctor.rule.wallWithoutRoom: Wall %1$@ (%2$@ m) does not border any room.
download.pdf.detail: One PDF floor plan per storey, in a ZIP.
download.svg.detail: One SVG floor plan per storey, in a ZIP – for drawing programs.
download.usdz.detail: The house as a 3D model for other apps and AR Quick Look.
download.zip.detail: The whole project with model and photos – opens in hAusbau on every device.
error.missingExample: The example model is missing from the app.
features.devices: Place outlets, switches, lights, sensors and more from a catalog, compare planned and placed quantities – the costs also count what is planned but not placed yet.
features.export: Export plans as PDF and SVG per storey or room, and whole projects as ZIP or USDZ.
features.extras: Notes, undo, a focus effect that points out what you picked, the Doctor's fixes, stairs, chimneys, storey adjustment, archive and settings.
features.import: Turns a 3-D model of your house (USDZ, e.g. from a LiDAR scan) into storeys, rooms and walls – or start from scratch and draw the walls yourself.
features.inspector: Inspector with rooms, walls, wiring, devices, costs and a Doctor that finds problems; show, hide, colour and fade everything – a storey's whole infrastructure at once, too.
features.lights: Simulate the lighting of a whole storey, room by room – lamps, pendants and the sun – with lux heat maps checked against recommendations.
features.network: Wi-Fi coverage of access points as a half sphere, and a network switch that shows its cable runs through the whole house
features.photos: Map photos of real walls onto the 3-D walls to keep track of what is behind the plaster.
features.templates: Four example templates: two houses, each as its USDZ or as a simplified floor plan with doors and windows
features.title: What hAusbau does
features.view: Explore the house in 3-D: orbit, zoom, jump to storeys and rooms, walk through rooms in first person, top-down, panorama or – on phones and tablets – by moving the device; choose which modifier keys move what, a table on the start screen lists every input.
features.walls: Edit walls storey by storey – move walls and nodes with a live preview –, add doors and windows, reshape or delete rooms and add new storeys with the storey below as a guide.
features.wiring: Plan power, lighting, network, water, heating and more: draw lines on walls and floors – with a preview –, add points, guide them along walls, floors and ceilings, edit types and notes.
gallery.empty: No screenshots yet – they are made by the tour's test run.
gallery.title: Screenshots from the Guided Tour
import.model.detail: A new project from a USDZ, USDA or USDC file – e.g. a RoomPlan scan of your house.
import.title: Import
import.zip.detail: A project exported as ZIP by hAusbau on any device.
intro.accessibility: hAusbau intro animation. Tap to skip.
lights.mixed: The lights differ – a change sets them all alike.
lights.model: Direct light, the ceiling's reflection of lamps shining up and the sun through doors and windows; walls block light – the values are conservative.
lights.none: No lights in this room. Place spots or lamps in Device mode.
lights.sunlit: The sun stands on this side
lights.title: Lights
line.hint.continue: Tap to continue the line along walls, ceiling and floor. Tap a point to join. Drag points to move them.
line.hint.select: Click a point to select it and drag it – with Shift only up/down (snapping to floor and ceiling), with Option/Alt only along its surface. A click on a line adds a point there. DEL deletes the selected point.
line.hint.start: Tap a wall, ceiling or floor to start a line – or tap a point of an existing line.
nav.action.moveNearest: the nearest node or wall follows
nav.matrix.footer: What the keyboard, the mouse and touch do in each view – as set in Settings, with the suggested default in brackets where it differs.
nav.matrix.title: Navigation
network.none: No outlet connected – place the switch at the rack, a riser or a cable trunk.
opening.dialog.footer: The object is placed in the middle of the wall; drag it to its final position.
opening.dragHint: Drag it in the 3D view to move it along the wall. It snaps to wall ends, neighbours and a 5 cm grid.
opening.name: Name
outline.hint: Drag the corners to fit the room. Tap a corner to select it.
panel.label: Label
panel.walls.opacityAll: Opacity of all walls on this storey
photo.hint: Pick a detected wall or drag the four corners onto the wall's corners. The photo is then straightened onto the wall.
photo.noCandidates: No wall detected automatically – drag the four corners onto the wall's corners.
photo.placement.hint: Drag the photo to move it, its edges or corners to resize it – or use the sliders.
photo.title: Match Wall
placement.device.ceilingOnly: This device can only be mounted on the ceiling
placement.device.floorOnly: This device stands on the floor
placement.device.more %@: Tap to place another %@, drag to move
placement.device.noWall: Tap closer to a wall – this device stands with its back against a wall
placement.device.wallOnly: This device can't be mounted there
placement.hint.drag: Drag or tap to move the note
placement.hint.tap: Tap a wall, ceiling or floor to pin the note
room.delete.message %lld %lld %lld %lld: The room holds %1$lld devices, %2$lld lines and %3$lld notes. “Delete Room” keeps them (without a room), the other choice deletes them too. Either way its own %4$lld walls go, with their doors and windows – walls it shares with another room stay; the floor follows the walls. Undo brings everything back.
selection.adjustHeight.mac: Hold Shift while dragging the device to change only its height.
selection.flipWallSide: Move to Other Side of Wall
selection.none.description: Tap a cable, device, note or wall in the 3D view.
selection.wall.photo.name: Photo name
settings.credits.footer: Each library ships inside the app named next to it; platform APIs belong to the OS or browser, the tooling is only used to build, test and develop.
settings.credits.nativeNone: The iOS/iPadOS and macOS app bundles no third-party libraries; all listed here ship with the web app.
settings.credits.platform: Platform APIs (part of the OS or browser, not bundled)
settings.debugLabels.footer: A bug at the lower left of the 3-D view and a small label at the end of the inspector name the mode, section, panel, camera, selection, what you are doing and the last control used. A click on the bug copies its text to the clipboard and shows it; the last line is the view link – in the web app it is also in the address, which opens the same view again. A click on the label copies it.
settings.focus.footer: Shown or selected elements get a pulsating, flashing border. The Focus button under “View” turns it on and off.
settings.input.footer: Which modifier selects which movement when dragging; picking one another movement has swaps the two. Invert turns the direction around: camera = looking around or turning the view, movement = walking or moving the house. Touch input stays as it is.
settings.keepAwake.footer: The screen doesn't dim or turn off while you use hAusbau.
settings.language.footer: The language applies right away and is remembered for you.
settings.lightLimit.footer: How many lights light mode shows in the 3-D view at most – the camera's room first, then the brightest. The heat maps always count every light. More lights can make the 3-D view slower.
settings.nav.hints.footer: Shows below the zoom slider what the keys, the mouse and touch do in the current view.
settings.nav.keyboard.footer: Which modifier key selects which movement with the arrow keys; picking a modifier another movement has swaps the two. Some combinations belong to the system or the browser (on the Mac, Control + arrows switches desktops).
settings.person.footer: Eye height in the first-person view. Space bar: jump (the taller, the higher). Toddlers crawl at half speed – and suck their pacifier instead of jumping –, giants walk on hairy feet.
settings.preview.detected.none: Press a key, drag or click in the view
settings.preview.footer: Hold modifier keys: the movements bound to them light up. Arrow keys, a drag, a right-drag or the wheel move the view as in the 3-D view – the row that reacted is framed, and “Detected commands” names the input and what it did (red: nothing is bound to it). Four walls stand around the die – the Walls settings show here too; a click selects the die or a wall. Top right where the camera is, bottom right what it looks at.
settings.preview.title: Try It Out
settings.resetPanels.footer: Puts the Build and View tools, the zoom slider, the edit cards and Settings back where they started.
settings.selectionMode.footer: “Switch to context mode”: selecting a wall, line or device while navigating opens wall, wiring or device editing right away – on its storey and in its room, the element stays selected.
settings.title: Settings
settings.walls.footer: Merging draws walls that meet or overlap – and the pieces around doors and windows – as one body. Merged lines outline a wall only along those merged walls, without lines where it runs into a neighbour. Simplified wall highlighting marks a selected wall with one flat rectangle in its plane instead of a box. Thin walls draw every wall as a thin sheet on the rooms' side, joined where walls meet. All of this changes only the drawing, never the walls.
stairs.hint: Tap the floor to place a flight (up to the next storey; next to a wall it lies against it); tap a flight to edit it, drag it to move it.
storeyAdjust.footer: Moves and resizes everything on this storey: walls, rooms, cables, devices, notes, doors and windows. Device sizes stay the same.
template.complex.detail: The 3-D scan as imported: every scanned wall piece, see-through walls.
template.simplified.detail: The same house with straight walls, doors and windows from the floor plan – all storeys, rooms, lines and devices. The scan stays available as an overlay in the wall editor.
template.title: Choose a template
template.twoStorey.detail: A second house, built from its floor plans: ground floor and attic with walls, door and window openings and every room, the open space over the kitchen – no lines yet.
template.twoStoreySimplified.detail: The same two-storey house as a wall plan: straight walls, doors and windows at the floor plan's sizes, the stairs, and rooms from the wall loops. The USDZ stays available as an overlay in the wall editor.
tour.addDevice.filter: Every device has its own icon, and the search field next to the title lists only the matching ones – here “spot”.
tour.addDevice.filterClear: An empty search field: all devices again.
tour.addDevice.kind: We take a floor lamp this time.
tour.addDevice.picker: “Place Device” at the top of the Devices section (or “+” › Place Device) opens the catalog; outlets have gangs and a height class.
tour.addDevice.room: To add a device, go to the kitchen and look from the top.
tour.addDevice.start: Place starts placing – or a second click on the chosen tile.
tour.addWiring.devicesOn: Devices are hidden while you draw lines – the wire editor’s Devices box brings back the outlets and switches the lines lead to …
tour.addWiring.draw: Each tap adds a point; the line follows walls and floors.
tour.addWiring.mode: Lines mode: choose the type – here a network cable.
tour.addWiring.second: New Line starts another one – a cold water pipe.
tour.camera.adult: Back at adult height (1.70 m) – space bar to jump here too.
tour.camera.backInRoom: Back into the living room – in the mode it was left in.
tour.camera.enterRoom: On a storey, the camera button with “…” enters the room in the middle of the view in first person.
tour.camera.eyeLevel: Next to the field of view: the next lower and higher eye level – from toddler to giant, as in Settings.
tour.camera.fov: The field of view is adjustable.
tour.camera.giant: As a giant (1.95 m) you stomp on hairy feet; the space bar jumps – the taller, the higher.
tour.camera.panorama: Panorama: the whole room at once.
tour.camera.panoramaZoom: In the panorama the arrow keys zoom; Shift + arrows look around.
tour.camera.rightWalk: Dragging with the right mouse button walks too – forward, back and sideways.
tour.camera.room: Inside a room the camera stands at eye height: first person.
tour.camera.roomStep: Over the lock the same: the previous and next room of this storey – quickly from room to room.
tour.camera.roomStepBack: And back to the living room. Under "Overview" small letters name the storey and room the camera is in – also while walking through doors and up stairs.
tour.camera.sticky: The lock keeps the camera in the room; then back to the overview.
tour.camera.switcher: The camera button shows the current view in its own colour. Over it, two smaller buttons slide out with the previous and next view – a click switches with a little projector click.
tour.camera.toOverview: The big camera button itself leaves the room for the overview; the camera modes are its small side buttons.
tour.camera.toddler: As a toddler (0.40 m) you crawl through the house with tiny arms – at half speed; the space bar makes the pacifier smack.
tour.camera.topDown: Top-down shows the room like a plan.
tour.camera.topDownPan: From above, the arrow keys move the view over the plan, as on a map; Shift + arrows turn and tilt it.
tour.camera.turnKeys: Shift + ←/→ turns the view on the spot, Shift + ↑/↓ tilts it.
tour.camera.walk: The arrow keys walk forward, back and sideways.
tour.camera.wheelZoom: The mouse wheel (or pinching) zooms – it narrows or widens the view.
tour.camera.worldRotate: “Rotate” works in the overview too: the house turns around the point in the middle of the view.
tour.chimney.add: Walls also take chimneys, through one or more storeys.
tour.devices.clear: Clear the selection and go back to the overview.
tour.devices.collapseAll: “Collapse All” folds every room of the list …
tour.devices.flip: A device on a wall moves to its other side – and into the room there.
tour.devices.fold: Each room of the device list folds by its head – handy in long lists.
tour.devices.inspector: The selection shows type, gangs, height, size, price and a note.
tour.devices.jump: A room from the list keeps the Devices section – its storey box follows to the room’s storey, only that storey is shown.
tour.devices.locate: Locate a four-way outlet in the kitchen.
tour.devices.tab: Devices on the ground floor, with planned and placed counts.
tour.devices.wiringOff: Right below “Place Device”: the storey, the devices – and the wiring, switched off here …
tour.doctor.dismiss: Or dismiss an issue you don't care about …
tour.doctor.fix: A fix solves it with one tap.
tour.doctor.fromEditor: From Wall Editing too: Issues closes the editor so the list can be shown.
tour.doctor.open: Back in the example house, the Doctor lists what doesn't fit.
tour.doctor.show: “Show” points the camera at the issue – only its “!” stays, highlighted and see-through, so the glowing parts behind it show.
tour.doctor.showAll: A tap in the 3-D view brings every “!” back.
tour.editWiring.alongWall: With Option/Alt it keeps to its surface – here it slides along the wall (pointer ↔).
tour.editWiring.drawTool: Back to Draw: with a mouse a faint line shows where the next click leads.
tour.editWiring.insert: A click on the line adds a point there (the pointer shows a “+”).
tour.editWiring.kind: Change its type – power, then speaker cable.
tour.editWiring.nodes: In Lines mode, drag a point to reroute the line.
tour.editWiring.placementCeiling: Ceiling: the line goes up the wall and across the ceiling – inside the storey's rooms only.
tour.editWiring.placementWall: “Placement” says where Draw puts points – Wall by default: seen from above a click goes onto the nearest wall, never off this storey. The surface a click would take is outlined, the line it adds shown as a ghost.
tour.editWiring.select: Tap a line to select it.
tour.editWiring.selectTool: Select and Draw, as in the wall editor. With Select a click picks a point – or adds one on a line.
tour.editWiring.shift: With Shift held the run stays level along the wall – or plumb, straight up or down.
tour.editWiring.storey: Its storey box works like the wall editor’s: another storey is edited and shown alone.
tour.editWiring.toWall: With Shift a point only goes up and down: on the floor it slides to the wall and sits at its foot – the pointer shows ↕.
tour.end.bye: That's the tour – have fun planning!
tour.end.finale: Bravo – you've seen everything hAusbau can do!
tour.end.gallery: The gallery shows pictures from this tour.
tour.end.navMatrix: At the bottom of the start screen, a table shows every view with what the keyboard, the mouse and touch do – as set, with the defaults where they differ.
tour.flatten.band: Lifted from the floor and lowered from the ceiling at once, the wall floats between both – each value applies while you type.
tour.flatten.do: Flatten turns them into a clean wall plan.
tour.flatten.editWall: “Edit This Wall” opens the wall editor with the wall selected.
tour.flatten.editWallDone: Done – back to the view from before.
tour.flatten.editor: Imported walls are uneven. In the wall editor, pick the upper floor.
tour.flatten.multi: Multiple selection is a checkbox of wall nodes: switched on, its three yellow nodes turn green.
tour.flatten.reference: The original walls can be shown for comparison.
tour.flatten.segment: Select a wall and set its thickness.
tour.flatten.segmentOpacity: Right below, the selected wall's transparency.
tour.flatten.wallBody: A wall is also selected by a click on its face – with a mouse it lights up yellow first and the pointer turns into a hand.
tour.flatten.wallFind: “Show in Walls Tab” jumps from the selected wall to its row and highlights it.
tour.flatten.wallInspector: Walls of a wall plan can be changed right in the inspector: length, height and thickness.
tour.flatten.wallLook: The selected wall's transparency and colour are right in the Selection tab.
tour.flatten.wallRow: The unfolded row edits the wall like the Selection tab: length, height, thickness – and shows its area.
tour.flatten.wallWindow: The selected wall gets doors, windows and chimneys right in the wall editor – and stays selected.
tour.focus.on: The Focus button makes the selection pulse so you can't miss it – the style is set in Settings.
tour.inspector.accordion: Expanded rows stay outlined and offer colour and name.
tour.inspector.circuit: The circuit is typed in – or picked from every circuit of the project.
tour.inspector.clear: The × on the Selection tab clears the selection.
tour.inspector.clickDeeper: … and once more the outlet – up to three behind the front one, then it starts over.
tour.inspector.clickFront: Aimed at the outlet, a click selects the wall in front of it …
tour.inspector.clickThrough: … clicked again at the same spot, the line behind it …
tour.inspector.contextMode: Settings › Selecting an element › Switch to context mode: a device picked, and device editing opens in its room – the device stays selected.
tour.inspector.contextModeBack: Back to “Keep selected mode”, the default.
tour.inspector.costs: Cost rows unfold into storeys and rooms.
tour.inspector.debug: “Debug Labels” shows a bug at the lower left and a small label at the end of the inspector – both say exactly where in the UI you are, e.g. for a bug report.
tour.inspector.debugClose: “Done” – or another click on the bug – closes the box again.
tour.inspector.debugCopy: A click on the bug spins it in rainbow colours, copies its text and shows it in the middle at once. The last line, the view link, describes the whole view; in a browser it is also in the address.
tour.inspector.fold: Storeys fold and unfold – the app remembers it.
tour.inspector.fullScreen: The full-screen button right of the zoom slider: on the Mac and in a browser the window fills the screen; on iPhone, iPad and touch devices the inspector and the top bar go. Blue while on.
tour.inspector.fullScreenOff: A second click ends full screen.
tour.inspector.hover: Pointing at a row outlines its element in 3-D.
tour.inspector.inspectorTab: The dark blue Inspector tab brings back the section's sheet – the selection keeps its own tab.
tour.inspector.items: The selection lists the room's other items – tap one to jump to it.
tour.inspector.itemsLocate: A click in “In This Room” selects the element and brings the camera there – so does Focus.
tour.inspector.modeFromSelection: With a wall selected, wall editing starts on its storey – also from the overview.
tour.inspector.place: Under the name: where the element is – its room and storey; a wall between rooms names all of them, separated by “|”.
tour.inspector.rename: The name is changed right in the selection – and it stays when you click elsewhere.
tour.inspector.renameBack: Left empty, the original name is back.
tour.inspector.roomMenu: The room is a menu of the storey's rooms: an outlet in the wall can belong to the room on the other side – the outlet itself stays where it is.
tour.inspector.sectionDevices: In Devices only devices: the same spot now selects the outlet. The selection is a tab on top of the sheet; the section stays lit.
tour.inspector.sectionWalls: In Walls a click selects only walls (and their doors, windows, chimneys) – aimed at the outlet, the wall is selected.
tour.inspector.selectionTab: A tap on the Selection tab flashes its icon and highlights the selection – as the Focus button does.
tour.intro.text: You will now be guided through hAusbau and all its features – the tour plays by itself. Watch the tour guide in the lower left: it explains each step. You can move it around, pause it and use it to jump forward and backward.
tour.intro.title: Guided tour
tour.lights.aim: “Aim the Sun Here” at a window: the sun stands square in front of it – the window glows, daylight shines into the room and onto the floor. (Also in a window's Selection tab while light mode is on.)
tour.lights.allLights: “All Lights of the Room” sets lumen, beam angle, colour temperature and colour of every light at once.
tour.lights.dim: The room dimmer dims all lights of the room.
tour.lights.emission: How it shines – circle, half-circle top or down – and its light colour.
tour.lights.heat: The heat map shows the lux on the work plane, with statistics; the legend marks the average and the maximum.
tour.lights.hover: Pointing at a light's row outlines it in the room; pointing at a light in the room marks its row.
tour.lights.master: “All Rooms” sets the dimmer of every lit room.
tour.lights.off: The × on the tab ends light mode; back to the overview.
tour.lights.pendant: A ceiling spot becomes a pendant lamp: it hangs on its cord below the ceiling.
tour.lights.pendantHeight: A pendant's height from the ceiling – a standing lamp has its height from the floor.
tour.lights.plane: The work plane can be raised and lowered – from the floor up to the ceiling; the heat map follows at once.
tour.lights.room: In the living room, Lights opens the “Light Properties” tab beside the selection: the storey goes dark, the room's lights shine.
tour.lights.storey: The lights are grouped by room: switch on the kitchen too – each lit room gets its own heat map.
tour.lights.sun: Ambient outside light: a sun shines in through the windows – its intensity, height and position on the dial.
tour.mini.none: No tour chapter for this view.
tour.mini.title: Tour of this view
tour.navigate.orbit: Drag in the 3-D view to turn the house. Under the zoom slider, small hints say what the keys, the mouse and touch do in this view.
tour.navigate.pan: Alt + arrow keys (or Shift + drag, right-drag, two fingers on touch screens) move the house across the floor – which modifier does what is up to you in Settings.
tour.navigate.tiltOver: Tilting with Shift+↑/↓ has no limit: hold it and the house turns over – here it stands on its head.
tour.navigate.zoom: Scroll or pinch to zoom in and out.
tour.navigate.zoomSlider: The slider in the middle at the bottom zooms too – in rooms it narrows the view.
tour.network.ap: A ceiling spot becomes an access point – through its type in the inspector.
tour.network.board: The main distribution board in the basement lists every circuit that reaches it through conduits and risers.
tour.network.circuit: A click shows the circuit: its lines, its devices and its way through all storeys down to the board.
tour.network.circuitDone: Another click turns it off again.
tour.network.done: Another click turns it off again.
tour.network.duct: Conduits and risers show which cables run through them – selected, those light up through all storeys.
tour.network.ductWiden: Back to 60 mm, everything fits again.
tour.network.ductWidth: The example's conduits are as wide as their cables need. Narrowed to 35 mm the cables no longer fit – the Doctor warns.
tour.network.highlight: A click on a connection shows its cable run through all storeys.
tour.network.riser: Risers are placed like devices, conduits drawn like lines; the layer “Conduits & risers” hides them.
tour.network.switch: A network switch at the rack: the inspector lists every outlet a cable leads to.
tour.network.wifi: Access points show their Wi-Fi coverage as a half sphere; the radius can be set.
tour.network.wifiOff: The layer “Wi-Fi coverage” turns it on and off for every access point.
tour.notes.compose: “+” › Place Note: write a note and pick its colour.
tour.notes.place: Tap where it belongs – it stays there in 3-D.
tour.notes.toggle: The note button hides all notes …
tour.openings.door: Add Door: size and depth, limited to what fits.
tour.openings.edit: The door's values can be changed afterwards.
tour.openings.leaf: A door can go without its leaf – then only the frame is shown.
tour.openings.outline: Edit Outline reshapes a room's floor: add points, drag them.
tour.openings.wall: Select a wall for a new door.
tour.pdf.end: Plans come per storey or per room, as PDF and as SVG.
tour.pdf.export: The storey's “…” exports it as a PDF plan with walls, lines and devices.
tour.photos.attach: Attach Photo: the app finds the wall's corners in the photo.
tour.photos.layer: Photo projection can be switched off and faded.
tour.photos.name: A photo is named after its file – type a new name right in the list.
tour.photos.place: Drag the photo or its edges on the preview – or move an edge with its slider.
tour.photos.placeUndo: The sheet has its own undo and redo, next to the tabs.
tour.photos.placement: “Placement” shows the wall in its real proportions, with the straightened photo, doors and windows.
tour.photos.projection: The selected wall's photos have the photo projection too: switch it off or fade it – the slider applies while you drag.
tour.photos.use: Use: the photo is straightened and laid onto the wall.
tour.photos.wall: Select a wall of the living room.
tour.photos.wallList: In the Walls tab a picture marks walls with a photo; the unfolded row adjusts it – like every wall's sizes.
tour.placeDevice.deleteKey: DEL deletes what is selected – devices, lines, walls, doors, windows, chimneys, notes and stairs; the inspector has a Delete button for it too.
tour.placeDevice.drag: In Devices mode, drag a device to move it.
tour.placeDevice.more: Every further tap places another one.
tour.placeDevice.tap: Tap where it goes – floor, wall or ceiling, as the device allows.
tour.placeDevice.wiresHidden: While editing devices the lines are hidden, so nothing covers the devices …
tour.placeDevice.wiresShown: … the Wires box in the Devices section shows them …
tour.projects.archiveView: The archive keeps old projects; restore or delete them for good.
tour.projects.delete: Delete forever, after a safety question.
tour.projects.model: “Import…” also creates a project from a 3-D model, here a USDZ scan.
tour.projects.plans: All plans of a project as PDFs, one per storey, in a ZIP …
tour.projects.rename: The project menu renames a project …
tour.projects.svg: … or as SVGs for drawing programs.
tour.projects.usdz: And the whole house back as USDZ.
tour.projects.zip: “Download…” offers every format of a project; the ZIP travels between all apps – “Import…” brings it back.
tour.rooms.back: … and “Back to” returns to the room you were in.
tour.rooms.go: “Go here” flies the camera into a room.
tour.rooms.jumpList: The chevron beside the navigation button opens a list of every room: first the rooms of the storey you are on, then each storey.
tour.rooms.jumpOther: … and another storey closes the first – only one is open at a time.
tour.rooms.jumpRoom: A room takes the camera there and closes the list; the button now names its storey.
tour.rooms.jumpStorey: A storey opens like an accordion and lists its rooms …
tour.rooms.overview: “Overview” goes back out to the whole house …
tour.rooms.storey: A whole storey can be focused too – the storeys above are cut away.
tour.scratch.deleteRoom: The “…” of a room deletes it. You choose: only the room (its devices and lines stay, without a room) or the room and everything in it.
tour.scratch.inner: Two inner walls split it into three rooms.
tour.scratch.names: Name them: hallway, kitchen, living room.
tour.scratch.new: A new empty project opens straight in the wall editor – with a metre grid and the Draw tool ready.
tour.scratch.rename: A click on a name in the list renames the storey, room, wall, line or device in place.
tour.scratch.rooms: Rooms from Walls creates the rooms.
tour.scratch.wiring: Run a power line through the rooms.
tour.settings.awake: Keep the screen awake while planning.
tour.settings.credits: Libraries & Tooling lists everything the app is built with.
tour.settings.focus: Focus styles from laser to unicorns, with a live preview.
tour.settings.invert: Every axis of the keyboard and the mouse can be inverted – separately for the camera and for movement.
tour.settings.lightLimit: “Limit of Lights”: how many lights light mode shows in 3-D – set to 4 and back to 12.
tour.settings.move: Dragging the grip or the title moves Settings sideways, so the 3-D model stays visible beside them. On phones they fill the screen.
tour.settings.navHints: “Show navigation hints” switches the small hints under the zoom slider on or off.
tour.settings.navMatrix: The navigation table is in Settings too, just above the libraries and licences.
tour.settings.navRole: Which modifier key selects which movement – for the keyboard and the mouse separately. Taking one another movement has swaps the two: the mouse's “Camera” takes Alt, “Self” gets none.
tour.settings.navRoleBack: And back to the suggested defaults.
tour.settings.open: Settings: language, keep the screen awake, focus style.
tour.settings.panning: Panning: camera-oriented, the arrow keys move the house; map-like, they move the view over it – the same in every view.
tour.settings.person: Settings choose the camera height: adult, giant, teenager, child or toddler.
tour.settings.resetPanels: “Reset Control Positions” puts moved tools, the zoom slider, the edit cards and Settings back in their places.
tour.settings.toys: Around the Settings card lie a few faded tools, candy and toy animals – placed anew every time (on phones behind the settings). A tap on the background shakes the card: everything falls out, flies off or sinks into the background, and a new set drops in from above or falls in from the front – some twirl on the way.
tour.settings.tryIt: Try it out: a die in a small 3-D view moves with the keys and the mouse as set above – Shift+↑ turns it here, and the “Camera” row is framed. Top right the camera position, bottom right the point it looks at.
tour.settings.walls: Walls: merge overlapping walls and their outlines, mark a wall with a flat rectangle, or draw thin walls – sheets on the rooms' side.
tour.short.lights.aim: Aim the sun at a window
tour.short.photos.name: Photo name
tour.stairs.add: The stairs tool places a staircase in the wall plan.
tour.stairs.climb: The ceiling is open above the stairs – in first person you walk up them to the next storey. The button at the top names the new storey.
tour.stairs.drag: With the Stairs tool a flight is dragged to its place: it snaps onto a wall it comes close to and stays in its room. The selected one is outlined in red, a flight under the pointer in yellow.
tour.stairs.edit: Set its steps; “Rotate” opens a dial that turns the flight around its centre – to any angle; next to a wall it lies against it.
tour.stairs.editButton: “Edit Stairs” opens the wall editor with the Stairs tool – the flight already selected.
tour.stairs.escape: Esc with the Stairs tool goes back to Select – the flight is no longer selected.
tour.stairs.mirror: “Mirror” keeps the flight where it is but turns it round: the top becomes the bottom.
tour.stairs.mirrorBack: Mirrored once more, it climbs as before.
tour.stairs.select: Outside the wall editor the flight can be clicked too (the pointer outlines it first): its inspector names room and storey, size, direction, steps and the storeys it connects.
tour.stairs.selectTool: With the Select tool a click on a flight switches to the Stairs tool; while drawing, you simply keep drawing.
tour.start.example: First we add the example project. hAusbau offers four templates: two houses, each as a complex USDZ or as a simplified floor plan.
tour.start.open: Open it: the 3-D view on the left, the inspector on the right.
tour.start.template: We take the complex USDZ: a complete house with four storeys, made from a 3-D scan. A project just added is outlined with the Focus effect chosen in Settings.
tour.start.welcome: Welcome! This tour shows everything hAusbau does – it plays by itself. Use Next to skip ahead, Back to repeat, Pause to stop.
tour.storey.add: Add a storey on top – the storey below shows through as a guide.
tour.storey.compass: The compass next to the zoom slider turns the plan around its centre – the red N always shows where north is.
tour.storey.deleteKey: DEL deletes the selected wall – like its Delete button.
tour.storey.drawCancel: Esc while drawing ends the wall following the pointer: the walls placed stay, a lone first node goes again.
tour.storey.drawLeave: Esc again switches to Select; Undo takes the test wall away.
tour.storey.editor: The wall editor shows a storey from above.
tour.storey.insertNode: A selected wall offers “Insert node here” where you touched it.
tour.storey.joinNode: Drag the new node close to a corner: it snaps on and joins it.
tour.storey.moveWall: A selected wall can be dragged; the walls joined to it follow as a preview until you let go. With a mouse: drag a wall directly, Ctrl moves what is nearest, Esc cancels.
tour.storey.moveWallAxis: With Shift held the wall keeps to one axis: dragged at a slant it only moves the way you drag further – down here.
tour.storey.roomName: The closed outline became a room right away – drawing ends, and you name it on the spot.
tour.storey.rooms: Rooms from Walls turns closed walls into a room.
tour.storey.tilt: Dragging turns and tilts the plan around the point where you grabbed it.
tour.storey.wallLines: “Wall lines only” hides the walls too – only the plan's lines at ceiling height are left.
tour.storey.wallTops: “Wall tops only” hides the floor – from above you see just the walls.
tour.storey.wire: A power line in the new storey …
tour.storeyAdjust.open: In the storey's “…”: Move & Resize Storey fixes a storey that is slightly off – with the Doctor's proposals.
tour.tabs.costName: Unfolded, a cost row shows its whole name. Planned devices that are not placed yet – in the example the smoke detectors, access points and Zigbee sensors – are listed under “Not yet placed” and counted in the total.
tour.tabs.costs: Costs: enter prices per metre or piece, the total updates right away.
tour.tabs.devices: Devices: planned against placed quantities, then every device by room.
tour.tabs.doctor: Doctor: finds problems like missing room outlines, with fixes; the “!” marks show where.
tour.tabs.structure: Rooms: storeys and their rooms; “…” on a row holds its exports.
tour.tabs.walls: Walls: every wall of a storey, with photo projection and transparency.
tour.tabs.wiring: Wiring: all lines by room, with their type and length.
tour.templates.add: The second template: the simplified floor plan.
tour.templates.open: The same house with the same rooms, lines and devices – but with straight walls, and doors and windows where the floor plan has them.
tour.templates.overlay: In the wall editor the scanned walls of the USDZ can be laid over the straight ones.
tour.templates.twoStorey: The second example house: two storeys built from its floor plans – here the USDZ as it is imported.
tour.templates.twoStoreySimplified: And as a simplified floor plan: doors and windows at the plan's sizes, plus the stairs up to the attic.
tour.undo.undo: Undo takes back the last changes …
tour.visibility.allRooms: “All” lists every room of the house – the same checkbox, so the kitchen is back in both lists.
tour.visibility.color: Expand a row to tint it, fade it or give it your own name.
tour.visibility.deviceGroups: Like “Lines”, “Devices” folds out its classes – here the lighting goes off, outlets and switches stay. “Conduits & risers” sits with the lines.
tour.visibility.infrastructure: The last row of every storey is its Infrastructure group: all its devices and lines at once. Hovering it outlines them, the eye hides them – walls and floors stay.
tour.visibility.infrastructureEdit: Expanded, it fades the storey's installation and takes your own name – every object keeps its own colour.
tour.visibility.infrastructureRestore: Back to full opacity and the original name.
tour.visibility.layers: The layers menu hides whole kinds of things – here all devices.
tour.visibility.layersHover: With a mouse, pointing at a layer shows only that kind of element – even when it is switched off; storeys carry their level, 0 at the bottom.
tour.visibility.lineGroups: Under “Lines” single groups can be hidden too – electricity, network, water, drainage, heating, climate, gas.
tour.visibility.oneFold: Only one fold-out is open at a time: “All” closes the storey's rooms. Leaving the menu brings back the view from before.
tour.visibility.restore: Reset the colour and show the storeys again.
tour.visibility.roomHover: Pointing at a room shows only that room – its walls, devices and lines – and frames it.
tour.visibility.roomSolid: A room's opacity is its walls' opacity: at 100 % they are solid – even the example's walls, which start at 30 %.
tour.visibility.storeyChecks: The storeys' checks in the layers menu are their eyes in the inspector: the upper floor shown there is checked here.
tour.visibility.storeyChecksBack: Pointing at “All” shows every storey for a moment; with the menu closed, the eyes count again – the upper floor off again.
tour.visibility.storeyEyeAbove: With one storey picked, the view leaves out everything above it. An eye that shows a storey above again really shows it: the view goes to the whole house for that.
tour.visibility.storeyHover: Pointing at a storey shows it alone and frames it – also a hidden one.
tour.visibility.storeyOnly: Below the layers are the storeys: a click shows only that storey and frames it.
tour.visibility.storeyPrevious: “Previous” restores the visibility of storeys and rooms from before the choice.
tour.visibility.storeyRooms: Each storey folds out its rooms: a checkbox hides one room.
tour.visibility.storeys: The eye hides a storey – here the attic and the upper floor.
tour.visibility.storeysAgain: For the next steps the upper floor and the attic are hidden again.
tour.visibility.walls: In Walls, the storey picker also takes the camera to that storey, and one slider makes all its walls transparent.
tour.visibility.wallsAll: A storey picked is shown alone – “All storeys” brings the others back, also those switched off in the layers menu (they are on there again).
tour.visibility.wallsLayer: Walls and floors can be hidden too – then lines and devices lie open.
tour.wiring.collapseAll: The rooms of the Wiring list fold too – all at once with one button …
tour.wiring.ethernet: A network cable in the living room.
tour.wiring.hideAll: Hide and show all lines of the list at once.
tour.wiring.light: Locate shows a line: the lighting circuit of the kitchen, outlined in 3-D.
tour.wiring.power: A power line – each type has its own colour.
tour.wiring.tab: Wiring, limited to the ground floor.
undo.flipWallSide: Move to Other Side of Wall
undo.label: Change Label
walls.compass: Compass: drag to turn the plan (red N = north)
walls.cutFilled: A door/window fills this cut – change its sill and height to adjust the cut.
walls.draw.hint: Tap to place nodes; each tap draws a wall from the last node. Tap a node or wall to connect. Once an outline is closed, “Rooms From Walls” turns it into rooms. Esc ends the wall following the pointer; Esc again switches to Select.
walls.flatten.hint: Flattening turns the imported wall slivers into clean walls with corner nodes. The USDZ file stays untouched.
walls.hasPhoto: A photo is mapped onto this wall
walls.hover.node %@: Click selects the node, then drag it · hold %@ to move what is nearest
walls.hover.stair: Click to edit this flight with the Stairs tool
walls.hover.wall: Drag to move the wall · Esc cancels
walls.node.hint: Drag the selected node to move its walls (snaps to 15/30/45/50/65/75/90°). Drop it close to another node to join them.
walls.roomMade: Room created – give it a name:
walls.segment.hint: Lift from ground and lower from ceiling together: when they overlap, the gap between is a cut for a window or door (a door/window added to this wall then fills it); otherwise the wall floats between them.
walls.select.hint: Tap a node or wall to select it, then drag it to move it; a selected wall offers “Insert node here”. Mouse: drag a wall (with Shift only along X or Y), hold Ctrl to move what is nearest, Esc cancels.
web.imageUnreadable: This browser can't read the image.
web.keepAwake.unsupported: This browser can't keep the screen awake.
web.notYet: %@ – not in the web app yet
web.phone.expanded: Show the inspector bar and sheet
web.phone.full: The inspector instead of the 3-D view
web.selectionNone: Click an element in the 3-D view to see its details.
web.storage: Projects are stored in this browser only. To continue in another browser or on the Mac/iPad app, export a ZIP and import it there.
web.storageTemporary: This browser may delete the data when space runs low – export important projects.
web.update.available %@ %@: A new version is available: you are running %1$@, the server has %2$@.
wireKind.speaker: Speaker Cable
